C1.label: D-e304c9

defects.summary: `CodexRuntime.QuotaKeyOf` is virtual and returns `codex`, and only `CustomCodexRuntime` overrides it. `DeepseekRuntime` (also a `CodexRuntime`, and registered by default) therefore files its refusals under `codex`, so a DeepSeek 'insufficient balance' refusal (a hopeless phrase) parks every Codex row with 'its Codex usage limit is spent', and a spent Codex quota parks DeepSeek rows in turn.

The locked write runs through `Task.Run(..., ct)` with the round's token. A round ended by its deadline or a stop therefore drops even parks that needed no probe (Claude, Codex, Kimi), and the log calls this 'the quota probe was cancelled', which is wrong. The plan only says that a cancelled probe parks nothing.
S33 checks the card's cooldown line against a date/time regex. The scenario asks for the exact S31 line.
S40 checks each edge-case verdict by the prefix of its record's `ToString()`, not by its type and value, so it asserts on text where behaviour is meant.
The cooldown file writes its instants with `ServerNotice.Iso` (milliseconds) but the wire and the sentence use a new `CooldownWords.Iso` (seconds), so one feature has two ISO formatters.
AGY_OLD is copied into a constant instead of being read from `fixtures/antigravity/consult-quota.stderr.txt`, which the plan names as its source. The bytes match today, but the copy can drift.

C1.summary: All of the plan's decisions are built and wired, with build, format and both suites green, and 42 scenarios passing by exact name plus S14 under a recorded longer name. They include the structured verdict, the agy readers keyed by bucket id, the locked fail-open cooldown file, aggregation per key after the round, roster exclusion, the providers member and the card; the deviations are recorded honestly, and an extra test runs a real round end to end. The main flaw is that DeepSeek inherits Codex's `codex` quota key, so either vendor's spent quota can keep the other's rows out; the remaining findings are a cancellation edge and some text-based or duplicated test details.

C1.label: D-1ff9e9

defects.summary: CodexRuntime.QuotaKeyOf answers "codex" as a virtual member and only CustomCodexRuntime overrides it, so DeepseekRuntime (also a CodexRuntime subclass, a separate API-key account) inherits the codex key: a DeepSeek refusal parks every codex row, and a DeepSeek answer lifts a real codex cooldown, which breaks D3's rule that a key belongs to one sign-in.

The test changes the zone by setting the TZ environment variable and asserts TimeZoneInfo.Local.BaseUtcOffset == +9 h, but .NET on Windows ignores TZ, so this test fails in ci.yml's windows-latest job, which runs the whole MCP suite (the objective run was Linux only).

The locked write runs as Task.Run(() => Apply(changes), ct) with the round's token, so a round that ends on its deadline or is cancelled also drops the codex, Claude and Kimi parks that needed no probe, where D5 makes only a cancelled probe park nothing.

For an agy model the table does not know, an undecided RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (Spent == null) goes to QuotaReset.FromText, whose word scan calls it hopeless and parks it on a guess, although D5/D10 say an undetermined agy refusal is never a parked row.

The guess-doubling count is worked out twice, once before the lock in ParkAsync and again under the lock in Change.Park.Applied, and CooldownWords.Iso repeats ServerNotice.Iso with a different precision.
S40's theory checks verdicts by ToString().StartWith rather than by value, and S33 checks the cooldown line with a regex instead of the exact S31 line.

CR1.label: D-a93f00

defects.summary: `Qualifies` filters agy's undecided refusals (`Spent == null`) through `RateLimit.Hopeless(reason)` before the gauge is asked, but D5 says the gauge decides agy's undecided case. An undecided `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` whose message has no spent word would never be probed or parked; every observed shape carries the status word, so this is latent.
The file is 463 lines, and the story-2 card says to split it into two once it passes 400 lines; §12 does not record this.
`DeepseekRuntime` overrides `QuotaKeyOf` to empty, which departs from D3 (`CodexRuntime` → `codex`, which it would otherwise inherit). The choice is sensible and tested, but §12 does not list it.

S35 asserts that B waits on the lock with `Thread.Sleep(300)` followed by `IsCompleted == false`. That is a timing-based check that can pass when it should fail, though the final both-keys assertion still catches an unlocked read-modify-write.
Its temp folders come from `Directory.CreateTempSubdirectory("coai-park-…")` rather than `TempDir.For("testsToDelete-quota-")`, which the plan's test rules require (existing tests do the same).
§12 says the plan's wording on `consecutive` made the doubling 'unreachable'. It overstates: that wording only delays the doubling by one park, which still justifies the change S39 needs.

C2.label: D-86888e
